userStories.title: Add stall detection wrapper for yt-dlp Python API download calls
acceptanceCriteria: Wrap ydl.download() call in download_segments.py with a concurrent.futures timeout mechanism
Timeout value is configurable via download config field segment_download_timeout (default 300 seconds)
On timeout, the download thread is interrupted and a DownloadError is raised with 'stall_timeout' category
Timeout errors feed into existing escalation/retry logic (not treated as network failure)
Unit test verifies timeout triggers after configured duration using mock ydl.download that blocks
Unit test verifies successful downloads within timeout are not interrupted
userStories.notes: Tier: P1 (hang prevention). Implementation was already in place from US-49-004: concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor wraps ydl.download() at line 782, config field is segment_stall_timeout (default 120s) in DownloadConfig. TimeoutError classified as 'timeout' category (not network/bot_detection). 14 unit tests added in tests/test_download_segments_stall_timeout.py covering: timeout triggers, successful download not interrupted, error classification, retry queue integration, network failure counter isolation, disabled mode, config defaults.

userStories.title: Fix iterative_match serialization to extract video_file from MatchResult structure
acceptanceCriteria: In iterative_match.py else branch (around line 452), drill into match.primary_match.video_segment.source_file when available
Fall back to getattr(match, 'video_file', '') only when primary_match is None or has no video_segment
Serialized matches with MatchResult objects produce non-empty video_file values
Unit test creates MatchResult with primary_match.video_segment.source_file set and verifies serialization extracts it
Unit test verifies fallback path still works for plain Match objects with video_file attribute
userStories.notes: Tier: P1 (data loss on restore). Files: src/stages/iterative_match.py:450-466. The else branch at line 452 does getattr(match, 'video_file', '') which always returns '' for MatchResult objects. The if branch (line 420-449) correctly drills into primary_match.video_segment.source_file — the else branch must mirror this pattern. Match.from_dict() rejects entries with empty video_file, so all iterative matches are silently lost on checkpoint restore.

userStories.title: Add network failure pattern tests for Python API exception format
acceptanceCriteria: Add test cases for _is_network_failure() with Python API exception message format (yt_dlp.utils.DownloadError wrapping)
Test covers 'Errno 11001' (DNS resolution failure) pattern matching
Test covers ffmpeg exit code 4294967158 (0xFFFFFEC6 = -314 signed) as network failure
Test covers 'Failed to resolve' hostname pattern
Verify _is_network_failure() returns True for all Python API formatted network errors
Add any missing patterns to _is_network_failure() if tests reveal gaps
userStories.notes: Added TestIsNetworkFailurePythonApiExceptionFormat class (17 tests) to test_error_classification.py. Added 'Failed to resolve' pattern to _NETWORK_FAILURE_PATTERNS (was missing — curl_cffi DNS failure). Tests cover: Errno 11001 in 4 wrapping formats, ffmpeg exit code 4294967158 in 3 formats, 'Failed to resolve' in 4 formats, plus 3 classify_error_category integration tests and 3 negative cases. All 78 tests pass.

userStories.title: Unify error classification between download_segments and core downloader
acceptanceCriteria: Extract _classify_error(), _is_network_failure(), _is_escalation_error() from download_segments.py into a shared module
Both download_segments.py and core.py import error classification from the shared location
Shared module lives at src/downloader/error_classification.py
Existing tests for error classification continue to pass after relocation
download_segments.py imports and delegates to the shared module (no duplicate logic)
core.py's ERROR_SEVERITY_PATTERNS are reconciled with _is_network_failure patterns
userStories.notes: Created src/downloader/error_classification.py with unified is_network_failure(), is_escalation_error(), classify_error_category(), classify_error_severity(), ERROR_SEVERITY_PATTERNS, SEVERITY_MULTIPLIERS, and threshold constants. download_segments.py imports _is_network_failure, _is_escalation_error, classify_error_category, NETWORK_FAILURE_THRESHOLD, BOT_DETECTION_ABORT_THRESHOLD from shared module. core.py imports ERROR_SEVERITY_PATTERNS, SEVERITY_MULTIPLIERS, classify_error_severity from shared module. All 365 relevant tests pass (7 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change).

userStories.title: Add bot-detection abort threshold to prevent futile download attempts
acceptanceCriteria: When consecutive_bot_detections exceeds bot_detection_abort_threshold (config, default 15), the stage aborts with a clear error message
Abort message includes the count of bot detections and recommends checking cookie config
Bot-detection errors do NOT reset the network failure abort counter (remove line 558-560 reset behavior if still present)
Unit test verifies stage aborts after threshold consecutive bot detections
Unit test verifies mixed bot-detection and success resets the counter
Bot-detection abort is logged as a stage-level failure with 'bot_detection_abort' category
userStories.notes: US-52-007 complete. Root cause: MagicMock escalation_result.tier.value > int comparison crashed in tests, preventing bot-detection counter from incrementing. Fix: (1) test mock get_escalation_args returns None to avoid MagicMock comparison, (2) added bot_detection_abort category to error_categories and error_aggregator when abort fires, (3) abort message includes count + cookie guidance, (4) added 3 new tests (abort category, abort message content, mixed success reset). All 75 related tests pass.

acceptanceCriteria: Integration test creates MatchResult objects with primary_match.video_segment.source_file populated
Test serializes matches through the ITERATIVE_MATCH checkpoint save path
Test deserializes via Match.from_dict() and verifies video_file is preserved
Test verifies download_segments._collect_matched_segments() correctly extracts video_id from restored matches
Test covers both MatchResult (with primary_match) and plain Match (with video_file) structures
Test file placed at tests/test_download_segments_restore.py
userStories.notes: Tier: P1 (data integrity). Files: src/stages/iterative_match.py:420-470 (serialization), src/stages/download_segments.py:458-489 (_collect_matched_segments), src/utils.py (MatchResult class), src/state.py (Match.from_dict). This is the end-to-end test for Issue 2 — ensuring the serialization-deserialization roundtrip preserves video file references so download_segments can actually find and download the matched segments.

userStories.title: Add config validation for download segment settings at pipeline startup
acceptanceCriteria: Pipeline startup validates download.cookies_from_browser is set when segment downloads are expected
Warning logged if cookies_from_browser is empty and no cookiefile/cookie_rotation is configured
Validation runs during DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS stage init (not at pipeline-level to avoid false positives for --match-only)
Unit test verifies warning is logged when no cookie source is configured
Unit test verifies no warning when cookies_from_browser is set
Validation does not block execution (warning only, not error)
userStories.notes: Tier: P2 (fail-fast diagnostics). Files: src/stages/download_segments.py (stage __init__ or run method), src/config/sections/download.py (cookies_from_browser field). Without cookies, every Python API download triggers bot-detection. This validation catches the misconfiguration early with a clear diagnostic message instead of letting the user discover it through N failed downloads. Warning-only because the user may intentionally rely on cookie_rotation or have cookies in another path.

userStories.title: Consolidate segment download stats tracking into a SegmentDownloadStats dataclass
acceptanceCriteria: Create SegmentDownloadStats dataclass with fields: succeeded, failed, cached, attempted, total, retry_count, segment_durations, total_bytes, error_categories, error_aggregator
Replace the inline stats dict in _download_segments() with the dataclass instance
Stats dataclass has increment_success(), increment_failure(category), increment_cached() methods
All stat access points in _download_segments and _print_progress updated to use the dataclass
Unit test verifies stat increment methods and field defaults
No behavioral change — purely structural refactor
userStories.notes: Tier: Refactor (type safety). Files: src/stages/download_segments.py:581-592 (stats dict), plus all references to stats['succeeded'] etc throughout the method. The current stats dict is initialized inline with 10+ keys and accessed via string keys throughout a 200+ line method. A dataclass provides IDE autocompletion, prevents typo bugs (stats['suceeded']), and makes the contract explicit.

Unit test verifies tier_distribution is correctly populated from mock escalation state

userStories.notes: Tier: Observability. Files: src/stages/download_segments.py (end of _download_segments before StageResult.ok), src/checkpoint.py (stage_metrics persistence). The escalation_summary already exists (line 449) but doesn't break down how many downloads used each tier. userStories.notes: Tier: Meta/config. Files: scripts/ralph/config/ralph-config.json (focusAreas, testPatterns, relevantFiles sections). The 'architecture' focus area exists in queue.json but not in ralph-config.json — it's not in the focusAreas array, testPatterns, or relevantFiles. This means Ralph can't auto-discover tests or files for this focus area. Adding it ensures future architecture sprints get proper test pattern matching and file discovery.
